The Attention Mechanism Work: The Attention Mechanism is a statistical technique that allows a model to focus on specific parts of the input data while ignoring others. It was introduced by Hochreiter et al. in 2001 as a way to improve interpretability and reduce overfitting in sequential models like RNNs. The basic idea behind the Attention Mechanism is to compute a weighted sum of inputs at each position in the memory cell, where the weights are determined by the importance of each input. This weighting scheme gives more importance to certain parts of the input when it comes to predicting future states, effectively "attending" to those areas first. ### How does the attention mechanism work and what are its applications work? (mechanisms and principles)
The Attention Mechanism is a key component of neural networks that allows them to focus on specific parts of a large input while ignoring others. It works by calculating the similarity between each token in the input and the current query token at every position in the text. This similarity score is then propagated through the network to produce weighted outputs that indicate how important each token is compared to the rest. The weights assigned to each token depend on the relevance of the corresponding query token to the current question. Applications of the Attention Mechanism include: 1. **Question Answering**: One of the most common use cases for the Attention Mechanism is in Question Answering (QA).
